group.passage: For decades, chlorofluorocarbons, or CFCs, seemed like ideal chemicals. They did not burn, were not poisonous, and hardly reacted with anything, which made them safe to use in refrigerators, spray cans, and foam packaging. Yet the very quality that made them so useful on the ground turned out to be a serious problem high above it. In 1974, two chemists at the University of California, Sherwood Rowland and Mario Molina, argued that CFCs last long enough to drift up into the stratosphere. There, strong ultraviolet (UV) light breaks them apart, setting free chlorine that destroys ozone. This matters because the ozone layer, roughly 7 to 25 miles above the ground, shields living things from harmful UV light, which can cause skin cancer. Makers of spray cans fought back hard, and at first the idea was dismissed even by some fellow scientists. In 1976, however, the National Academy of Sciences confirmed their findings, and in 1978 the United States banned CFCs in spray cans. The most alarming evidence arrived in 1985, when researchers from the British Antarctic Survey reported that ozone over Antarctica was disappearing every spring. Satellite data then confirmed that this “hole” stretched across the whole continent. In 1987, countries responded with the Montreal Protocol, an agreement to phase out CFCs and other chemicals that harm the ozone layer. It later became the only United Nations treaty accepted by every country on Earth, and about 99 percent of the substances it controls have now been phased out. Even so, the damage cannot be undone quickly. Because CFCs break down so slowly, some kinds stay in the air for around a hundred years. Scientists expect the ozone layer over most of the world to return to its 1980 condition around 2040, over the Arctic around 2045, and over Antarctica not until about 2066, and only if every country keeps its promises. The Antarctic hole has grown smaller and shallower since 2000, though its size still changes a great deal from year to year. There is a further twist. Some chemicals that replaced CFCs do little harm to ozone but trap heat strongly, so in 2016 countries agreed to cut those as well. Solving one problem, it turns out, means watching closely for the next.

options.A: They caught fire easily once they had risen into the upper air.
options.B: They were poisonous to anyone who breathed in the spray.
options.C: They trapped heat and slowly made the whole planet warmer.
options.D: They were stable enough to reach the upper air and release chlorine.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the Montreal Protocol?

options.B: It eventually won the support of every nation in the world.
options.C: It was signed soon after the United States banned CFC sprays.
options.D: It was first suggested by the scientists who studied Antarctica.

translation_zh.text:
數十年來，氟氯碳化物（CFC）看起來是理想的化學物質。它們不會燃燒、沒有毒，而且幾乎不和任何東西起反應，所以用在冰箱、噴霧罐和泡棉包裝裡都很安全。然而，正是這個讓它們在地面上如此有用的特性，後來在高空成了嚴重的問題。
1974 年，加州大學的兩位化學家羅蘭（Sherwood Rowland）和莫利納（Mario Molina）提出，CFC 存在得夠久，能飄進平流層。在那裡，強烈的紫外線會把它們分解，放出會破壞臭氧的氯。這件事很重要，因為位於地面上方約 7 到 25 英里的臭氧層，能保護生物免受有害的紫外線傷害，而紫外線會導致皮膚癌。噴霧罐製造商強力反擊，起初連一些科學界同行也不接受這個看法。然而，美國國家科學院在 1976 年證實了他們的研究結果，美國也在 1978 年禁止噴霧罐使用 CFC。
最令人震驚的證據出現在 1985 年：英國南極調查局的研究人員發現，南極上空的臭氧每年春天都在消失。衛星資料隨後證實，這個「破洞」橫跨整個南極大陸。1987 年，各國以《蒙特婁議定書》回應，同意逐步停用 CFC 和其他破壞臭氧層的化學物質。它後來成為唯一被世界上每個國家都接受的聯合國條約，它所管制的物質如今約有 99% 已經停用。
即使如此，損害還是無法很快修復。由於 CFC 分解得非常慢，有些種類會在空氣中留存約一百年。科學家預期，如果每個國家都信守承諾，世界大部分地區上空的臭氧層會在 2040 年左右回到 1980 年的狀態，北極上空約在 2045 年，南極上空則要到 2066 年左右。南極臭氧洞自 2000 年以來已經變小、變淺，不過它的大小每年仍有很大的變化。
還有一個轉折。一些取代 CFC 的化學物質對臭氧的傷害很小，卻會強烈吸收熱，因此各國在 2016 年同意也要削減這些物質。看來，解決一個問題，就得密切注意下一個問題。

problems: 第三段「It later became the only United Nations treaty accepted by every country on Earth」：與事實單 f11 以及 NOAA、BAS 的說法一致，但事實單同時引用的 UNEP 臭氧秘書處（s5）寫維也納公約與蒙特婁議定書「Both have achieved universal ratification, with 198 Parties」，所以 the only 嚴格說不精確（宜改成 the first United Nations treaty 或 one of the only treaties）。不影響任何小題（第 2 題正解 B 只需要「每個國家都接受」），列 warn 供人工審核，改版時建議修正並在事實單 f11 加註
details.method_zh: 逐句比對選文、圖表（caption、description、chart 數值）、題幹與選項中的事實與數字和事實單；圖表數值重新下載來源資料比對；可開啟的來源逐條確認（見各條 note）。
